mutations.because: the trailing `/` goes, and this is the ONE widening in the file, so the separator is the only thing between a purge and a campaign nobody named. `org/<org>/campaign/<uuid>` is a prefix of `org/<org>/campaign/<uuid>x/inputs/a` — a sibling campaign whose uuid merely BEGINS with this one — and the two callers D243 allows are a purge (PT-9g) and a reconciler (PT-9h), for which "is a prefix of" means "is deleted". `assertObjectKey` cannot catch it: a key with no trailing separator is still a legal key, so the mutant passes every check the builder makes and only the neighbour test sees it. That test asserts both halves on purpose — the sibling key does not start with the prefix, AND it does start with the prefix minus its last character — so the mutant cannot pass by having become a prefix of nothing.

the campaign id stops going through `segment`, so nothing checks it before it joins a namespace a purge will empty whole. The witness is a SLUG: `summer-sale` is alphabet-legal, so `assertObjectKey` accepts `org/local/campaign/summer-sale/` and the refusal never happens — the builder returns a well-formed key into a namespace no write will ever populate, which is DoD 3 failing silently (nothing a user can rename may sit in the store's namespace, and a slug is renameable by definition). `..` is the wrong witness here precisely because `assertObjectKey` WOULD have refused it: the second validator exists to catch the one shape the port's own rule admits, and only a slug-shaped id demonstrates that this builder's own check was load-bearing rather than decorative.
